summary: Code notebooks for the book Hands-On Large Language Models, chapter by chapter from tokens and embeddings to RAG and fine-tuning.

heroCommands.command: Open any chapter notebook in Google Colab

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: This repository holds the code for every example in the book Hands-On Large Language Models. There is a notebook for each of its 12 chapters: language model basics, tokens and embeddings, how transformers work, text classification, clustering and topic modeling, prompt engineering, advanced text generation, semantic search and RAG, multimodal models, building embedding models and fine-tuning.
sixtySeconds.problem: Learning LLMs from theory alone is hard. These notebooks let you run each concept from the book and see the results.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for well-explained, chapter-ordered notebooks that the authors built and tested on free Google Colab GPUs.
requirements: Or a local Python setup using the repo's setup guide

overview: The authors recommend running the examples in Google Colab, which offers a free T4 GPU with 16GB of VRAM. Each chapter has an Open in Colab link in the README.
For local use, the .setup folder has a quick-start guide and the conda folder has a full environment guide including PyTorch.
There is also bonus content in the bonus folder. The code is Apache 2.0 licensed; the book itself is sold separately.
